title: AL Object ID Ninja: An Apology, a Decision, and a Month on the House
summary: The author of AL Object ID Ninja, which already went commercial after four self-funded years, is ending private self-hosted backend support and closing the source code. He says this is because an established BC company bundled its own Ninja-compatible backend into its paid offering. Private backend users get a one-month grace period on the commercial platform, or they can turn off auto-update and keep their current extension version.
key_points: AL Object ID Ninja was free for four years but became unsustainable due to growing infrastructure costs
A third-party company bundled Ninja-compatible backend access with their own paid offering, routing around the commercial service
Private backend source code is no longer open and self-hosting is no longer officially supported
Users with private backends get one month free access to the commercial platform to migrate, or can stay on their current extension version
The decision prioritizes sustainable development funding while unfortunately affecting users with legitimate operational reasons for self-hosting

quotes.text: For four years, I ran the backend out of my own pocket.
quotes.why_it_matters: Establishes the creator's personal financial commitment and context for why changes were necessary

quotes.text: I just can't afford to be anyone's fool.
quotes.why_it_matters: Captures the emotional and practical justification for closing self-hosting to prevent further exploitation
